clue.text: Movingly clasped an artist's work

indicators.note: movingly suggests the letters of the following words are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone describes how a painting tenderly took hold of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movingly' reads as emotion but asks for the letters of CLASPED AN to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting of countryside scenery is a classic kind of picture an artist produces.

clue.text: My word! An outstanding nut!

indicators.note: read as out-standing: the word An stands on the outside of the exclamation

parts.note: taken as written
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my word

explanation.surface: An excited cry at finding a really superb nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' is split as out-standing, so A and N stand outside COR, a British cry of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit of the oak tree is a classic example of a nut.

clue.text: Simple task to introduce direct debit into state benefit

indicators.note: into says the banking abbreviation goes inside the welfare payment

parts.note: the dole is British slang for state unemployment benefit
DD is the standard British abbreviation for a direct debit

explanation.surface: Paying welfare by automatic bank transfer is said to be easy.
explanation.walkthrough: The DOLE is British slang for unemployment benefit; a DD (direct debit) is an automatic bank payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A British colloquialism for something very easy to do, a piece of cake.

clue.text: Work at last-assemble hastily

definitions.meaning: a last is a shoemaker's foot-shaped form, so working at one means mending shoes
to put together roughly or in a rush

explanation.surface: A hurried assembly done at the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' reads as 'finally' but is the shoemaker's form.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend shoes is to cobble them, and to cobble something together is to throw it up crudely in a hurry.

clue.text: In the paper, I learn of danger

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of letters in the next few words

explanation.surface: Someone reads about a threat in the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril and danger are straightforward synonyms for risk of harm.

clue.text: Factor finds conditions are terrible

indicators.note: terrible suggests the preceding words are in a bad way and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: An analyst reports that bad conditions are a factor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' signals an anagram of CONDITIONS ARE; 'finds' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken into account when deciding is a consideration, a factor.

clue.text: Illness from a germ salesmen spread

indicators.note: spread suggests the letters are scattered and laid out afresh

explanation.surface: Travelling salesmen spread a germ and cause sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like the germ spreading, but it signals rearranging A GERM SALESMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubella is the viral illness also known by this two-word name.

clue.text: All cargo bays unlocked? It's a free-for-all

definitions.meaning: a whimsical literal reading: the holds of a ship have no bars across them

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a fight with no restrictions, and literally ship holds not barred shut.

clue.text: 11 covered in part of text for minister's address

indicators.note: covered in says one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: a page is one part of a written text
the answer to 11 across, a firing offence, is the crime of setting fires

explanation.surface: A cross-reference hidden in a passage locates where a clergyman lives.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' points to the answer at 11 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicarage or rectory, the home provided for a clergyman, is his official residence.

clue.text: This could spring a nasty surprise on Mickey

definitions.text: This could spring a nasty surprise on Mickey

parts.words: This could spring a nasty surprise on Mickey
parts.note: Mickey is the famous cartoon mouse, and the device springs shut on a rodent

explanation.definitionFit: A spring-loaded device for catching small rodents would indeed shock a cartoon mouse.

clue.text: A firing offence

parts.note: usually a sackable misdeed at work, here read literally as a crime involving setting fire

explanation.definitionFit: The criminal act of deliberately setting property alight is literally a firing crime.

clue.text: Sort of dancing — get arm round

parts.note: an arm is a limb
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A dance teacher tells someone to put an arm around a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean dance in which performers bend backwards under a low bar.

clue.text: Female always has illness

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A woman is perpetually sick.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised body temperature is a common sickness or symptom.

clue.text: Spread quickly round the East

indicators.note: round says the word for speedy goes around the compass point

parts.note: fast means quickly
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Something spreads rapidly around the eastern region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a verb but is a noun, a lavish meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is a lavish banquet of food laid out.

clue.text: It may be extremely visible before sunrise

definitions.text: It may be extremely visible before sunrise

indicators.note: extremely takes only the extremes, the first and last letters of the word
in a down clue, rise means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something shines brightly in the sky just before dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'sunrise' is split in two, and 'rise' works as an upward-reading signal because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The planet often seen as the morning star shines brightly in the eastern sky before dawn.

clue.text: Out of practice? Try us out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone lacking recent practice invites a test.
explanation.definitionFit: Skills that have lapsed through disuse are rusty, like corroded metal.

clue.text: Seat a little comfortless -add leather

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Advice to make an uncomfortable seat better by adding leather.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle is the seat a rider sits on, on a horse or bicycle.

clue.text: Tips us to wait in

indicators.note: in says the word for waiting goes inside the pronoun

parts.note: taken as written
to pend is to wait, remain undecided

explanation.surface: Someone advises a group to wait inside, or receive a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' looks like gratuities but is a verb meaning overturns.
explanation.definitionFit: Tips over is the same as turns upside down.

clue.text: A long time divided about name for girl

indicators.note: the long period is split apart and placed about the abbreviation

parts.note: ages means a long time

explanation.surface: A girl's name has been split up over a long period.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional female first name.

clue.text: Rears sharks

definitions.meaning: brings up or tends, as with children
a kind of shark found in warm coastal waters

explanation.definitionFit: To nurse is to bring up or tend, and nurse sharks are a familiar species.

clue.text: Gift of ancient money

definitions.meaning: a unit of weight and currency in the ancient Greek and Roman world

explanation.surface: A present of old coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural gift or flair, and also a sum of money in antiquity, as in the biblical parable.

clue.text: Giving a good smack?

parts.note: smack reads as a hit, but here means a flavour, so something with a good flavour

explanation.definitionFit: Food that is full of flavour is delicious or appetising.

clue.text: Alters details of people in advertisements

indicators.note: in says the word for persons goes inside the word for adverts

parts.note: ads is short for advertisements
men means people

explanation.surface: Someone changes the particulars of the people shown in commercials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'details of' is a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to change or modify, especially a text.

clue.text: Drum used in nursery rhyme opening?

definitions.meaning: the start of the rhyme beginning ..., the piper's son

explanation.surface: A drum is played at the start of a children's song.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom-tom is a hand-beaten drum, and the nursery rhyme about the piper's son opens with the doubled name.

clue.text: Rise and dress

definitions.meaning: to get out of bed or stand up
an outfit, often an odd or showy one

explanation.surface: Getting out of bed and putting on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To get out of bed in the morning, and an outfit or costume, often an outlandish one.

clue.text: The tiniest spot of colour in the garden

definitions.text: The tiniest spot of colour in the garden

parts.words: The tiniest spot of colour in the garden
parts.note: a small coloured part of a flower, one of the smallest bits of colour in a garden bed

explanation.definitionFit: One of the coloured leaf-like parts of a flower's corolla is a tiny fleck of colour in a garden.

clue.text: Finished a course of Italian

parts.note: past means over, finished
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has completed an Italian language course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course of Italian' suggests a language class, but it is a course in an Italian meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti, penne and the like form a typical dish served at an Italian meal.

clue.text: In mine, look for guide

indicators.note: in says the old word for look goes inside the mine

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone down a mine searches for a guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot steers ships into harbour, so a pilot is a guide.

clue.text: She may take the palm for her foresight

definitions.text: She may take the palm for her foresight

parts.words: She may take the palm for her foresight
parts.note: taking the palm usually means winning a prize, here read literally as holding a hand to read the future

explanation.definitionFit: A palmist predicts the future by holding a client's hand, taking the palm literally.

clue.text: Fellow-student makes grade with success at chess

parts.note: a class is a grade or rank
mate, short for checkmate, is the winning move at chess

explanation.surface: A fellow pupil earns a good mark and wins at chess.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in the same school class or year is a fellow pupil.
